title: Achebe: The Novel That Let Africa Tell Its Own Story

lines: One novel let the whole world hear Africa's own voice.
Who changed the world today? November 16.
Who changed the world today? November sixteenth.
96 years ago today,
Ninety-six years ago today,
a boy was born in Nigeria.
He was Chinua Achebe, father of modern African literature.

data.name: Achebe

lines: Born in Ogidi, in eastern Nigeria,
he grew up between Christianity and Igbo tradition.
In 1948, he entered University College, Ibadan,
In nineteen forty-eight, he entered University College, Ibadan,
and read Western books where Africans were silent extras.
He decided Africa's stories should be told by Africans.
In 1958, he published his first novel, Things Fall Apart,
In nineteen fifty-eight, he published his first novel, Things Fall Apart,
about an Igbo warrior's world, falling apart under colonial rule,
about an Igbo warrior whose world falls apart as colonizers arrive,
since translated into over forty languages.
He liked to quote an African proverb:
until lions have historians, hunting tales glorify the hunter.
until the lions have their own historians, the story of the hunt will glorify the hunter.
In 1975, he challenged Conrad's classic, Heart of Darkness,
In nineteen seventy-five, he challenged Conrad's classic, Heart of Darkness,
saying it reduced Africans to a dehumanized backdrop.

lines: Later, a car crash left him paralyzed from the waist down,
but in America he kept teaching and writing.
In 2007, he won the Man Booker International Prize,
In two thousand seven, he won the Man Booker International Prize,
and he died in Boston in 2013, at eighty-two.
and he died in Boston in twenty thirteen, at eighty-two.
Today, students around the world still read Things Fall Apart.
He let Africans tell their own story, in their own voice.
So here is his question:
If others keep telling your story, will you take back the pen?
